_comment: EXAMPLE · Kafka source (@stream_publisher) — payload FORMATS, BATCH axes and the dead-letter topic, each CHECKED. data_format and schema are BOTH always required ("json" + a JSON Schema, "avro" + an Avro schema, Protobuf(message_name=...) + the .proto source) and the schema is ENFORCED, not documentation. Messages are buffered and written to parquet files per the tabsdata.kafka.buffer.* keys; three batch axes on the decorator decide when the written files are staged as one batch, whichever fires first once batch_min_secs (60 seconds) have passed since the last batch: batch_max_rows (read_json), batch_max_secs (read_timed), batch_max_bytes (read_avro). dlq_topic (read_dlq) keeps one bad message from stopping ingestion. One function per file under functions/kafka_src/; the dead-letter reader is functions/caps_kafka_topics.py::kafka_dead. WHERE THE MESSAGES COME FROM: the domain's data plane writes the employees model as JSON (the seed, then a batch to employees and departments, every other departments row without the dept_name read_dlq requires -- --schema-changes drop -- so those go to <prefix>.dead), and scripts/produce_events.py writes the events read_avro and read_protobuf read: 50 Avro events (binary, no header) to <prefix>.avro_events and 50 com.example.UserEvent messages to <prefix>.proto_events, the domain's data plane writing JSON only -- BEFORE the publishers are registered, so their topics exist when the consumers subscribe (one subscribed to a topic that does not exist yet sees it only at its next metadata refresh, 30 seconds by default). Everything sent is appended to ${xp:dir}/ops.jsonl. read_timed needs its OWN collection (same topic as read_json; a second consumer in one group on a one-partition topic would sit idle); publishers on different topics share a group, which rebalances cooperatively by default, and a publisher whose partition is taken away stages and acknowledges what it holds first, so another one registering never makes it stage the seed twice. CHECKS (scripts/verify_kafka.py, tagged check, polling at most 20m): employees, avro_events, proto_events each hold their topic's messages exactly once; departments the ones that validate and kafka_dead the rest (--require-dead); employees_timed every employees message. Topics are ${D0__DB} references, so two runs never share one. Run: `tdd xp one-shot --suite kafka/kafka_src --keep`.
